exposure: Prenatal external anal sphincter (EAS) EMG amplitude asymmetry
outcome: Reduction of EAS EMG amplitude after delivery
cohort: Two hundred and forty-five pregnant nulliparous women were recruited at their second and third trimester of pregnancy, with a subgroup of 167 women followed after delivery.
finding: The reduction of external anal sphincter (EAS) EMG amplitude after right episiotomy was larger in women with right asymmetric sphincter compared with women with left asymmetry and women with other types of delivery.
mod_finding: The reduction of external anal sphincter (EAS) EMG amplitude after right episiotomy was larger in women with right asymmetric sphincter compared with women with left asymmetry and women with other types of delivery, suggesting a personalized approach to episiotomy might be beneficial.
